messages:
Maya: Quick sync request — need to finalize the onramp lanes for Merchant Cohort A. Main questions: required benchmarks, pin policy options for early customers, and deprecation notice windows. Can we align on these today? Context: ACME pilot expects deterministic latency and a stable model across updates.

Alex: Proposed lanes: `beta` (opt-in), `committed` (contracted capacity + SLA), `legacy` (deprecated model for customers who bought long-term pins). For `committed` we should require: p99 latency < 250ms (edge-case), p90 < 150ms, and no regression on the ACME prompt set for 7 days post-rollout.

Sam: Eval plan: we'll add the ACME prompt set, a general commerce set, and a fuzzing suite for structured outputs. Metrics: hallucination rate (<2% for committed), slot accuracy / F1 for structured fields, and generation token quality (logprob thresholds) — not just perplexity. Also add per-prompt variance checks.

Jordan: Note from sales: ACME asked to keep v1 pinned until their cutover window. We can offer pin exceptions. Need to decide on two modes: `soft-pin` (traffic defaulted to pinned model but customers can opt into new) vs `hard-pin` (no auto-switch until expiry). Legal wants explicit billing language for hard pins.

Evan: Comms perspective: recommend two collateral pieces: 1) onboarding guide - how to opt into new models and pin controls, 2) deprecation notice template (90/60/30 day cadence). Also a merchant-facing FAQ about expected behavior during canaries and rollbacks.

Maya: Canary/runbook question — Alex, what do you propose for ramp steps and rollback gates?

Alex: Canary flow suggestion: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Durations: 24h, 48h, 72h, 7 days. Rollback triggers: any single-step spike in p99 above 20% of baseline OR error rate > 0.5% OR a quality regression on the ACME eval set above threshold. Example config snippet: ```yaml
canary:
  - step: 1
    duration: 24h
    metrics:
      - p90_latency < 150ms
      - errors < 0.5%
  - step: 10
    duration: 48h
    metrics: same
```

Sam: Add an automated eval check at each step: run the post-deploy prompt set (sampled) and fail if hallucination or structured-field F1 degrade beyond the defined guardrail. Tag results to the deployment so we can trace regressions to model artifacts.

Maya: On pinning: my proposal — default to `soft-pin` for all non-enterprise; allow `hard-pin` as a contract add-on with SLA delta and fee. Also add a migration runway: if a model is deprecated, give pinned customers a 180-day grace window + migration support.

Jordan: Sales feedback: they'll accept soft-pin for most SMBs, but top 5 merchants want hard-pin. Need pricing buckets for hard-pin + migration assistance. I'll draft options with legal.

Evan: Marketing to prepare a short help center article and a one-pager for account teams. Also prepare a merchant-facing timeline template with the 90/60/30 day cadence.

Alex: Blockers: infra capacity for `committed` dedicated pools. I'll open a quota request to eng-infra and include traffic profile.

deploy-bot: Canary job started by Alex at 1712350500 — canary-id: canary-1712350500.

Maya: Action items: Alex — finalize canary config + open infra quota ticket; Sam — finalize eval sets and threshold table; Jordan — contract text for hard-pin + pricing; Evan — draft comms and FAQ. Sync Wed 10am. Anyone object? @everyone :thumbsup:
